decisions.decision: The entity check is advisory, never blocking
decisions.rationale: These are drafts and a human reads every line; a blocking gate would stop an edition over a token the reviewer was about to fix. What matters is that it is INVOKED.

decisions.decision: A lane that cannot fail must not report a pass

decisions.decision: null and undefined do not collapse in an edition record

context_notes: Nine commits across three PRs (#22, #23, #24), CI green on each, production smoked. The through-line of the second pass: every gate I shipped in the first pass reported CLEAN somewhere it had no power to fail. A --no-llm run logged '0 ungrounded findings, 42 tokens checked' and not one of the 42 could have been missing, because the summary IS its own source. The ADR-001 comparison was against a byte-220 slice rather than against a competent fallback — a measurement of how little effort had gone into the alternative, not of the LLM. And one of my own assertions passed by coincidence: 'ends with a letter' is not 'ends mid-word', and it was blind to the exact mutation it existed for. All three were found by pointing an instrument at real data or by mutating it, never by re-reading it.
